questions.question: You have an Azure solution that uses a virtual network, a storage account, and multiple virtual machines. You need to recommend a solution to log information about IP traffic entering and leaving the virtual network. Which type of logging solution should you recommend?
questions.rationale: Virtual network flow logs are used to log IP traffic information. Activity logs are used to log control plane events for individual Azure resources in a storage account, but it does not cover IP traffic. Application Insights logs data from applications. Azure Storage Analytics logs events related to storage accounts only. [Azure security logging and auditing | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/security/fundamentals/log-audit) [Design network solutions - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-network-solutions/)

questions.question: You have an Azure App Service web app named App1. You need to recommend a diagnostic logging solution to ensure trace and debug events are logged for app1. Which level of logging should you recommend?
questions.rationale: Verbose adds debug and trace messages to the log. Error logs error and critical messages, not debug and trace messages. Warning adds warning messages to the log. Information adds information messages to the log. [Enable diagnostics logging - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/troubleshoot-diagnostic-logs) [Design a solution to log and monitor Azure resources - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-solution-to-log-monitor-azure-resources/)

questions.question: You have an Azure virtual network named VNet1. You plan to store VNet1 diagnostics data. You need to recommend a solution for storing diagnostic data that meets following requirements: - Provides high-speed access to all logs - Keeps all logs for five years - Ensures that logs entries cannot be modified Which two options should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.rationale: Immutable Storage legal hold and Premium Blob storage ensure that logs are held for the required time and are stored immutable, meaning they cannot be changed once stored. Archive and Cool access tiers will not be suitable where high-speed access to all logs is required. [Design for Azure Monitor Logs (Log Analytics) workspaces - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-solution-to-log-monitor-azure-resources/3-design-for-log-analytics)

questions.question: Your organization has multiple Microsoft Azure resources spread across different regions. Each team manages its own set of resources. You need to design a solution that allows centralized monitoring while respecting the autonomy of each team over their data. Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.rationale: To achieve centralized monitoring while respecting team autonomy, configure Data Collection Rules (DCRs) to control data ingestion into a centralized workspace, ensuring only relevant data is collected. Implement a centralized Log Analytics workspace with role-based access control (RBAC) to provide a unified view of logs and metrics while maintaining data security. Use Azure Monitor Workbooks to create interactive dashboards that consolidate data from various sources, offering a comprehensive view of resource performance. Implementing multiple Log Analytics workspaces with separate access controls leads to fragmented data management, using Azure Policy to enforce monitoring standards is more about governance than performance monitoring, and using Azure Monitor Alerts does not directly contribute to centralized monitoring. [Design a solution to log and monitor Azure resources - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/design-solution-to-log-monitor-azure-resources)

choices.text: Configure Data Collection Rules (DCRs) for data ingestion into a centralized workspace.
Implement a centralized Log Analytics workspace with role-based access control (RBAC).
Implement multiple Log Analytics workspaces with separate access controls for each team.
Use Azure Monitor Alerts to notify teams of resource issues.
Use Azure Monitor Workbooks to create dashboards from different sources.
Use Azure Policy to enforce monitoring standards across all resources.

selectedAnswers.text: Configure Data Collection Rules (DCRs) for data ingestion into a centralized workspace.

correctAnswers.text: Configure Data Collection Rules (DCRs) for data ingestion into a centralized workspace.
Implement a centralized Log Analytics workspace with role-based access control (RBAC).
Use Azure Monitor Workbooks to create dashboards from different sources.

questions.question: You have an application that runs on load-balanced Azure virtual machines. The application must access an Azure storage account and an Azure Key Vault. You need to recommend an identity strategy for accessing Azure resources. The solution must meet the following requirements: - Secure access to the resources based on permissions. - Minimize the number of identities to create. Which type of identity should you include in the recommendation?
questions.rationale: You create a single managed identity and assign it to virtual machines and permissions. Using system-assigned managed identities create one identity for each virtual machine and those identities must be added to permissions for each resource accessed by the virtual machines. Microsoft Entra ID users and groups requires creating the users and the group manually. [Managed identities for Azure resources - Microsoft Entra | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/active-directory/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview) [Design managed identities - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-authentication-authorization-solutions/9-one-design-managed-identities)

questions.question: You need to design an identity solution for Azure virtual machines. The solution must meet with the following requirements: - Identities must be removed when virtual machines are deleted. - Identities cannot be shared among multiple virtual machines. Which type of identity should you use?
questions.rationale: Using system-assigned managed identities will create one identity for each virtual machine and delete the identity when the resource is deleted. User-assigned managed identities can be shared. Using Microsoft Entra users or groups requires you to manually delete users and the group. questions.question: You need to design a solution to store keys used by an application hosted in Azure. The solution must meet the following requirements: - Be compliant with FIPS 140-2 Level 2 - Be optimized for costs - Be fully managed Which key management solution should you use?
questions.rationale: Key Vault Premium is fully managed and FIPS 140-2 Level 2. Key Vault Standard is not FIPS 140-2 Level 2. Managed HSM is level 3, higher than 2, but it is more expensive than Key Vault. Self-hosted HSM is not fully managed. questions.question: You are designing an authentication solution for a hybrid environment that spans Azure and on-premises datacenters. You need to use Microsoft Entra ID to authenticate remote users accessing applications on-premises. What should you include in the design?
questions.rationale: Application Proxy allows on-premises applications to use tokens from Microsoft Entra ID. Windows Hello for Business is used for multi-factor authentication (MFA) on Windows clients. Microsoft Entra Verified ID is incorrect. Microsoft Entra DS is a managed Active Directory service in the cloud. questions.question: You are migrating an on-premises application to Azure. The application is deployed to three Azure virtual machines that are each configured as web servers. The application manages its own users and passwords. The application requires permission to access Azure resources. Each web server must use the same identity to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID. What should the web servers use to authenticate?
questions.rationale: User-assigned managed identities automate credential rotation and can be applied to multiple resources. Service principals depend on secrets that expire and do not have automatic credential rotation. System-assigned managed identities apply to single resources and will not work for three web servers. A username and password do not provide automatic credential rotation. [Design service principals for applications - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-authentication-authorization-solutions/9-two-design-service-principals)

questions.question: You need to recommend a solution that allows you to verify which Azure resources do not have tags. The solution must not block users from creating new resources. What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.rationale: Including Azure policies with an audit effect will run the policies but does not block users from creating resources that are noncompliant. Including Azure policies with a disabled effect will not run the policies. Including resource groups with a delete lock prevents deletions. Including resource groups with a read-only lock prevents the creation of resources. [Understand how effects work - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effects) [Design for resource tags - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-governance/6-design-for-resource-tags)

Azure Policy with an audit effect
resource groups with a delete lock
resource groups with a read-only lock

questions.question: You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com. You have an Azure subscription named Sub1. You create two groups named Group1 and Group2. You need to control access to Sub1 to meet the following requirements: - Ensure that the users in Group1 can grant permissions to Azure resources. - Ensure that the users in Group2 can reset a user’s password. - Follow the least privilege principle What should you do for Sub1?
questions.rationale: **Objective:** 1.3 Design governance **What This Item Tests:** Recommend a solution for identity governance **Additional Reading:** [Design for resource tags - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles%20https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/secure-best-practices#identity-governance) **Rationale:** Assigning the Owner role to Group1 and the Helpdesk Administrator role to Group2 allows Group1 to manage Azure resources and grant permissions, while allowing Group2 to reset user passwords. The Contributor role does not allow permission assignment, and the Authentication Administrator role can set or reset any authentication method (including passwords) for non-administrators and some roles.

choices.text: Assign the Contributor role to Group1 and the Authentication Administrator role to Group2.
Assign the Contributor role to Group2 and the Authentication Administrator role to Group1.
Assign the Owner role to Group1 and the Helpdesk Administrator role to Group2.
Assign the Owner role to Group2 and the Helpdesk Administrator role to Group1.

selectedAnswers.text: Assign the Contributor role to Group1 and the Authentication Administrator role to Group2.

correctAnswers.text: Assign the Owner role to Group1 and the Helpdesk Administrator role to Group2.

questions.question: Your organization plans to deploy a new web application that requires high availability and scalability, handling HTTP and HTTPS traffic within your existing Azure infrastructure. You need to select an Azure container service with built-in load balancing, custom domain support, and managed TLS for Azure FQDNs and custom domains. What should you recommend?
questions.rationale: Azure App Services web app is the most suitable choice as it provides built-in load balancing, supports custom domains, and offers managed TLS for both Azure FQDNs and custom domains. Azure Kubernetes Service, while popular, requires additional configuration for TLS management, making it less suitable for this requirement. questions.question: You are designing an Azure App Service web app named WebApp1. The headers and footers of the web pages delivered by WebApp1 will contain large amounts of static HTML. You need to recommend a solution to provide the greatest responsiveness for WebApp1. What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.rationale: The primary way to improve the responsiveness of WebApp1 is to avoid having it constantly calculating and delivering static content. Azure Cache for Redis is designed to eliminate most of this overhead. Traffic Manager, deployment slots, and Azure Load Balancer do not directly address the responsiveness requirement. [Design a caching solution - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-application-architecture/6-design-caching-solution)

questions.question: You have an Azure App Service web app that stores data in Azure SQL Database and uses Azure Cache for Redis as a distributed cache. You need to reduce the number of requests sent to Azure SQL Database. The solution must minimize development effort. What should you implement?
questions.rationale: **Objective:** 4.2 Design an application architecture **What This Item Tests:** Recommend a caching solution for applications **Additional Reading:** [Cache-Aside pattern - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/cache-aside) **Rationale:** A Cache-aside pattern is correct because it minimizes development effort while reducing database load. It does this by retrieving data from the cache when available and only querying Azure SQL Database on cache misses, and then populating the cache. Geo-replication for Azure SQL Database improves availability and read locality but is not primarily a caching strategy. Multiple App Service instances scales compute but does not reduce database requests unless paired with an effective caching pattern. Multiple Azure Cache for Redis instances might improve cache scalability but typically requires application changes to distribute keys across instances and is not the simplest approach for minimizing development effort.

questions.question: You need to design a file storage solution in Azure. The solution must meet the following requirements: - Provide the highest possible durability. - Remain available during a zone or Azure region failure. Which type of redundancy should you use?
questions.rationale: Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS) provides zone and region redundancy, and the highest durability. Locally-redundant storage (LRS) provides redundancy at the zone level. Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) provides redundancy at the region level. Geo-redundant storage (GRS) provides redundancy for region failure, but not at the zone and region level. [Data redundancy - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy) [Design for data redundancy - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-data-storage-solution-for-non-relational-data/4-design-for-data-redundancy?ns-enrollment-type=learningpath&ns-enrollment-id=learn.wwl.design-data-storage-solutions)

questions.question: You need to design a data analysis solution in Azure that meets the following requirements: - Allows for data transformation - Links data to Microsoft Power BI - Performs near real-time log analysis What should you use?
questions.rationale: Azure Synapse Analytics allows you to transform data, links data to Power BI, and performs near real-time log analysis. You cannot do near-real time log analysis in Data Factory. You cannot perform near real-time analysis in Azure Cosmos DB or SQL Managed Instance. [What is Azure Synapse Analytics? - Azure Synapse Analytics | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/synapse-analytics/overview-what-is) [Design a data integration and analytic solution with Azure Synapse Analytics - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-data-integration/5-solution-azure-synapse-analytics)

questions.question: You have an Azure subscription. You need to configure an Azure compute solution that meets the following workload requirements: - Full control is not required. - High-performance computing (HPC) is required. What should you use?
questions.rationale: Azure Batch is the correct answer as it provides HPC resources without the complexity of full control. Virtual machines require full control and are not related to any workload requirements in the scenario. Azure Functions does not provide HPC, and either does Azure Container Instances. [Choose an Azure compute service - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-compute-solution/2-choose-compute-service)

questions.question: You are designing a large-scale microservices-based application. A message queue will be used to hold unprocessed messages. Each message will be processed once, and then deleted from the queue. Each message will be approximately 32 KB in size. At peak periods, up to 10 million messages might be unprocessed. Which messaging service should you recommend for the application?
questions.rationale: A message queue is needed to meet the processing requirement. The key limitation in this situation is the volume of data. Ten million 32-KB messages exceeds the 80 GB limit for Service Bus. [Design a messaging solution - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-application-architecture/3-design-messaging-solution)

questions.question: You are designing an Azure solution that contains the following resources: - A virtual network with an Azure firewall - A virtual machine scale set running an application - Two virtual machines that run Microsoft SQL Server You need to provide management rights to different teams for the virtual network, scale set, and database servers. The solution must minimize administrative effort. How should you organize the solution components?
questions.rationale: Using a different resource group for each solution component allows you to provide RBAC access at the resource group level and does not require any extra Azure components. You cannot assign RBAC roles based on tags without additional administrative effort. Using a different management group for each solution component requires different subscriptions for each set of components, a virtual network in each subscription, and peering. Using a different subscription for each requires different subscriptions for each set of components, a virtual network in each subscription, and peering. [Organize your Azure resources effectively - Cloud Adoption Framework | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/azure-setup-guide/organize-resources) [Design for resource groups - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-governance/5-design-for-resource-groups?ns-enrollment-type=learningpath&ns-enrollment-id=learn.wwl.design-identity-governance-monitor-solutions)

questions.question: You have five Azure SQL databases in a resource group named RG1. You have a Log Analytics Workspace named WS1. WS1 is configured to use resource-context access mode. questions.rationale: Reader role for WS1 provides the required permissions. [Design for Azure Monitor Logs (Log Analytics) workspaces - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-solution-to-log-monitor-azure-resources/3-design-for-log-analytics)

questions.question: You are planning the deployment of an Azure Storage account that will host a file share. You need to recommend the storage tier for the account. The solution must provide the lowest possible latency for file access. While storage tier should you recommend?
questions.rationale: Azure Files offers four tiers of storage: Premium, Transaction optimized, Hot, and Cool. The lowest latency is offered by the premium tier. [Design for Azure Files - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-data-storage-solution-for-non-relational-data/6-design-for-azure-files)

questions.question: You are designing a hybrid network for an organizational migration to Azure. Some resources will be deployed to Azure. Other resources will remain on premises. You need to recommend a solution to connect the on-premises network to Azure. Which two services should you use to connect the networks? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
questions.rationale: ExpressRoute is the high-speed option for extending your on-premises network to Azure. No data travels over the public internet. You can use a VPN gateway to tunnel on-premises network traffic to Azure, while using the public internet as a backbone. VPN Gateway can be used as a backup for ExpressRoute. [Design patterns for Azure network connectivity services - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-network-solutions/4a-design-patterns-for-azure-network-connectivity-services)

questions.question: You have an Azure App Service web app named App1 in a resource group named RG1. You need to live stream log events for App1. Which CLI command should you run?
questions.rationale: `az webapp log tail -g rg1 -n app1` starts live streaming of events. `az webapp log show -g rg1 -n app1` shows log configurations, not live events. `az webapp scan start -g rg1 -n app1` starts a log scan on a web app, not live streaming. `az webapp scan list-result -g rg1 -n app1` Get details of all scans conducted on web app. [Enable diagnostics logging - Azure App Service | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/troubleshoot-diagnostic-logs) [az webapp log | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/webapp/log?view=azure-cli-latest) [Design a solution to log and monitor Azure resources - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-solution-to-log-monitor-azure-resources/)

questions.question: You are designing a data storage solution in Azure. The solution must meet the following requirements: - Provide read and write region replicas with eventual consistency. - Store non-relational data. What should you include in the design?
questions.rationale: Azure Cosmos DB provides read and write replicas with eventual consistency and can store non-relational data. Azure SQL Database, Azure Synapse Analytics, and SQL Managed Instance do not provide read-write replicas across regions with eventual consistency. [Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels) [Design for Azure Cosmos DB and Table Storage - Training | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/design-data-storage-solution-for-relational-data/9-design-for-azure-cosmos)
